Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

GALVANIZED STEEL WIRE STRAND FOR 

SIGNALLING PURPOSES 

( First Revision ) 



i 



(O 



1. Scope — Covers requirements for galvanized steel wire strand for signalling purposes. 

2. Ter minology — The terms given In IS : 2363-1965 ' Glossary of terms relating to wire ropes ' and 

the following shall apply. 

2.1 Bundle — Shall mean two or more coils properly bound together. 

2.2 Co/7 — Shall mean one length of wire or strand In the form of a coll having a mass of 50:t2'5 kg. 

2.3 P/ece — Shall mean a length of wire without joint or splice of any description in the finished 

wire. 

3. Dimensions 

4. Material 

4.1 The wire shall be manufactured from steel made by open hearth, electric duplex, basic-oxygen or 
a combination of these processes. In case any other process is employed by the manufacturer, 
prior approval of ttte purchaser should be obtained. 

4.2 If so required, the manufacturer shall furnish the steel maker's cast analysts to the purchaser 
and issue a certificate to him that the wire has been drawn from the certified steel. 

4.3 The steel used shall be plain carbon and shall not contain sulphur and phosphorus more than 
0050 percent each. 

4.4 The wire shall be coated with zinc of Grade " Zn d8*' of 13:209-1066 'Specification for zinc 
( second revision }\ 

4.5 The general requirements for the supply of materials to this standard shall be In accordance with 
IS: l387-tS67 'General requirements for the supply of metallurgical materials {first revision)*. 

5. Grades — The grade of a strand is the minimum tensile strength in N/mm' of the wires comprising 
the strand and shall be one of the following: 

Grade Tensile Strength Range of Wire 

N/mm« 

800 800 to t 000 

950 950 to 1 tSO 

1 too t too to 1 300 

f. Requirements 

6.1 Construction — The wire strand shall consist of six cover wires and one core wire 
[1x7 (6/1)]. 

i.2 Lay of Strand — The wires shall be stranded in right-hand direction and the maximum length of 
lay shall be 70 mm. 

6.3 Galvanizing — The galvanized coating of steel wire shall conform to the requirements in Table 1.

6.4 Mass — The signalling wire strand shall be in the form of a coil of one length having a mass of 
50 ± 2*5 kg. 

7. FrMdom from Defects 

7.1 The wire shall be circular in section and free from scale, inequalities, splits and other defects- 
The zinc coating shall be smooth, even and bright. 

7.2 Each length of wire shall be warranted to contain no weld, splice or joint whatsoever other than 
in the rod before it is finally drawn. 

6. Tests 

t^l Sampling 

6.1.1 Sampling for cfiemical analysis ^ Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the 
supplier, one test for chemical analysis shall be conducted for each lot or batch of coils manu- 
factured from a particular cast or a group of casts at the option of the purchaser. 

8.1.2 Sampling for mechanical test — Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the 
supplier, one sample shall be selected from each lot or batch of 20 coils or part thereof. 

8.1.2*1 Samples for mechanical test shall be cut from one end, or both the ends In case of 
doubt, of the selected coils from each batch, of sufficient length for the test of the wire and also for 
the re-test, if required. 

8.1.3 /?e*<e5fs-- Should any one of the test pieces first selected fall to pass any of the tests 
specified, two further samples shall be selected for testing in respect of each failure. Should the test 
pieces from either of these additional samples fall, the material represented by the test samples 
shall be liable to rejection, as not conforming to this standard. 

8.2 Tensile Strength, Maximum Elongation and Breaking Load ^The material, when tested in accor- 
dance with IS : 1521-1972 ' Method for tensile testing of steel wire ', shall have the physical properties 
given In Table 1. 

8.3 Reverse Bend Test — Test samples when tested in the manner described in IS : 1716*1971 ' Method 
for reverse bend testing of steel wire ( first revision ) * shall withstand, without brealiing or showing 
sign of splitting or other defects, the number of bends specified in Table 1. 

8.4 Wrapping Test of Steel — This shall be conducted in accordance with IS : 1755-1961 ' Method for 
wrapping test of wire '. The wire shall stand being wrapped eight times around Its own diameter 
and subsequently unwrapped without showing signs of fracture. 

8.5 Coating Test — The mass and uniformity of zinc coating shall be tested by the methods specified 
in IS: 4626-1968 ' Galvanized coatings on round steel wires *. 

8.6 The requirements pertaining to the adhesion of zinc coating shall conform to IS : 4826-1968. 

§. Marking — Each coil shall be provided with a label fixed flrmiy on the Inner part of the coll» 
bearing the following Information: 

a) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark, 

b) Lot number and coil number, 

c) A brief description and quality of the material, 

d) Mass, and 

e) Any other particular specified by the purchaser, 

9.1 ISl Certification Mark — Details available with Indian Standards Institution. 

1 



18:2285-1978 

10. Packing — Each coil shall be delivered securely bound with four separate binders of galvanized 
wire of size not less than 2-00 mm. The wire shall be smoothly and uniformly coiled so that the 
inner diameter of the coil shall be about half a metre. The coils shall then be wrapped individually 
•n stout hessian or other suitable material. If required by the purchaser, the coils shall be suitably 
weather protected, by dipping three times in boiled linseed oil or by any other process, after having 
been bound, but before being covered with hessian or other suitable material and labelled. 



I 

EXPLANATORY NOTE ^ 

This standard was first issued in 1983. The experience gained In the Implementation of this 
stanctord since Its Issue necessitated the present revision. Table t has been completely revised 
and requirements pertaining to minimum mass of zinc coating and number of dips before and after 
stranding have also been included in the table. 

The grade numbers have been changed and the new grades 800, 900 and 1 110 correspond to 
1, 2 and 3 respectively of 1983 version of the standard as for the minimum breaking loads are 
concerned. All the values have been given in SI units. 

Galvanized steel wire strands are used in large quantities by the railways for signalling 
purposes. This is an item which Is subjected to intermittent shock loadings as well as the corrosive 
action of the atmosphere. So the need was felt for maintaining a uniform level of quality in the 
wire as well as its anticorrosive coating. This standard is a step towards fulfilling this need.
